question.:question/problem:
A storage tank initially holds $600\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $23\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved stabilizer.
A feed solution containing $0.04\,\text{kg/L}$ of the stabilizer is pumped into the tank at a rate of $15\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $10\,\text{L/min}.$
Find, rounded to two decimal places, the amount of stabilizer in the tank $10$ minutes after pumping begins.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.04\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(15\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.04\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(15\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.6\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=600+15t-10t=(600+5t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{600+5t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(10\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{600+5t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(10\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{600+5t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{10Q}{600+5t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{2Q}{120+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.6-\frac{2Q}{120+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{120+t}Q=0.6.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 2/(120+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{2\ln|120+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (120+t)^{2}}\\&=(120+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(120+t)^{2}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(120+t)^{2}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{120+t}Q)&=(120+t)^{2}\cdot 0.6\\
(120+t)^{2}\frac{dQ}{dt}+2(120+t)^{1}Q&=0.6(120+t)^{2}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(120+t)^{2})&=0.6(120+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(120+t)^{2})\,dt&=\int 0.6(120+t)^{2}\,dt\\Q(120+t)^{2}&=0.6\cdot\frac{1}{3}(120+t)^{3}+C\\Q(t)&=0.2(120+t)+C(120+t)^{-2}.\end{aligned}$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=23.$ Thus,
$$\begin{aligned}0.2(120+0)+C(120+0)^{-2}&=23\\
24+C(120)^{-2}&=23\\C(120)^{-2}&=-1\\C&=-14400.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$Q(t)=\frac{t}{5} + 24 - \frac{14400}{\left(t + 120\right)^{2}}.$$
Finally, the amount in the tank $10$ minutes after pumping begins is
$$\begin{aligned}Q(10)&=0.2(120+10)-1(\frac{120}{120+10})^{2}\\&=26-1(\frac{12}{13})^{2}\\&\approx 25.15\,\text{kg}.\end{aligned}$$
This is rounded to two decimal places.

question.:question/problem:
A storage tank initially holds $100\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $6\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved stabilizer.
A feed solution containing $0.07\,\text{kg/L}$ of the stabilizer is pumped into the tank at a rate of $12\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $8\,\text{L/min}.$
Find, rounded to two decimal places, the amount of stabilizer in the tank $24$ minutes after pumping begins.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.07\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(12\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.07\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(12\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.84\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=100+12t-8t=(100+4t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{100+4t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(8\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{100+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(8\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{100+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{8Q}{100+4t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{2Q}{25+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.84-\frac{2Q}{25+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{25+t}Q=0.84.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 2/(25+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{2\ln|25+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (25+t)^{2}}\\&=(25+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(25+t)^{2}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(25+t)^{2}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{25+t}Q)&=(25+t)^{2}\cdot 0.84\\
(25+t)^{2}\frac{dQ}{dt}+2(25+t)^{1}Q&=0.84(25+t)^{2}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(25+t)^{2})&=0.84(25+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(25+t)^{2})\,dt&=\int 0.84(25+t)^{2}\,dt\\Q(25+t)^{2}&=0.84\cdot\frac{1}{3}(25+t)^{3}+C\\Q(t)&=0.28(25+t)+C(25+t)^{-2}.\end{aligned}$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=6.$ Thus,
$$\begin{aligned}0.28(25+0)+C(25+0)^{-2}&=6\\
7+C(25)^{-2}&=6\\C(25)^{-2}&=-1\\C&=-625.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$Q(t)=\frac{7 t}{25} + 7 - \frac{625}{\left(t + 25\right)^{2}}.$$
Finally, the amount in the tank $24$ minutes after pumping begins is
$$\begin{aligned}Q(24)&=0.28(25+24)-1(\frac{25}{25+24})^{2}\\&=13.72-1(\frac{25}{49})^{2}\\&\approx 13.46\,\text{kg}.\end{aligned}$$
This is rounded to two decimal places.

$$V(t)=400+20t-30t=(400-10t)\,\text{L}.$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.6-\frac{3Q}{40-t}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{40-t}Q=0.6.$$

$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 3/(40-t)\,dt}\\&=e^{-3\ln|40-t|}\\&=e^{\ln (40-t)^{-3}}\\&=(40-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}(40-t)^{-3}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{40-t}Q)&=(40-t)^{-3}\cdot 0.6\\

$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 1/(80+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{1\ln|80+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (80+t)^{1}}\\&=(80+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}(80+t)^{1}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{80+t}Q)&=(80+t)^{1}\cdot 0.4\\

$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.05\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.4\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=320+8t-4t=(320+4t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{320+4t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(4\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{320+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(4\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{320+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{4Q}{320+4t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{1Q}{80+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.4-\frac{1Q}{80+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{80+t}Q=0.4.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 1/(80+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{1\ln|80+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (80+t)^{1}}\\&=(80+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(80+t)^{1}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(80+t)^{1}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{80+t}Q)&=(80+t)^{1}\cdot 0.4\\
(80+t)^{1}\frac{dQ}{dt}+1(80+t)^{0}Q&=0.4(80+t)^{1}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(80+t)^{1})&=0.4(80+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(80+t)^{1})\,dt&=\int 0.4(80+t)^{1}\,dt\\Q(80+t)^{1}&=0.4\cdot\frac{1}{2}(80+t)^{2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.2(80+t)+C(80+t)^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$

$$Q(t)=\frac{t}{5} + 16 - \frac{1104}{t + 80}.$$

$$\begin{aligned}Q(5)&=0.2(80+5)-13.8(\frac{80}{80+5})^{1}\\&=17-13.8(\frac{16}{17})^{1}\\&\approx 4.01\,\text{kg}.\end{aligned}$$
